messages:
Alexa Chen: Hi team — taking over as PRIMARY for US-EAST for this window. I’m picking up an active pager (p99 token gen latency). Briefing: incident-bot flagged increased latency starting ~10m ago, some 5% error spikes for a small subset of customers. I’m going to run through quick checks and handoff notes below.
Jordan Patel: Thanks Alexa. I’ll stay secondary and monitor customer error rates + support tickets. ETA on the first triage?
Alexa Chen: V quick: 1) tail inference logs on rt-infer-prod-us-east 2) check kvcache hit rate 3) verify autoscaler didn’t spike churn. Commands I ran: ```kubectl -n inference logs -l app=rt-infer --tail=200 | grep p99```
Samir Gupta: noted. If kvcache hit-rate < 85% consider forcing a cache warmup route. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-warmup
incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager: HIGH p99 latency on text-generation-us-east • 5% errors • Rate increased x3 • Affected: public-hosted customers. Incident ID: INC-20260315-022
Mia Torres: Customer impact check: Support queue shows 7 tickets referencing timeouts in last 12m, top customer ids: cust_42, cust_77. I’ll message support with status. Also putting a banner on status.redwood.ai: partial degradation for text generation in US-EAST.
Alexa Chen: Quick mitigation checklist (doing now):
- Scale up primary pool by +2 GPUs (if capacity) using dedicated-autoscaler -> `rt-infer--scale 2 --region us-east`
- If long tail persists, fallback route to lower-cost quantized variant: model=v1-q4f16
- If KV cache cold, run cache warmup job: `jobs/run-cache-warmup --model rt-base --region us-east`

I’ll attempt scale first.
Jordan Patel: If scaling won’t bring p99 < 800ms in 3m, switch routing to v1-q4f16 for non-enterprise customers. I’ll take the routing flip if you give the go.
Alexa Chen: Scale issued — `cli:dedicated scale` returned job 8342 -> nodes provisioning. Watching.
Samir Gupta: While we wait, background checks: kube events show a flurry of pod OOMKilled 12m ago in the inference-autoscaler. Might be a memory regression in the recent sidecar change. Link to runbook for pod restarts: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pod-oom-restart
Mia Torres: Support updated and status banner live. Noting enterprise customers on dedicated instances are unaffected per monitoring (only hosted pool).
incident-bot: [UPDATE] Autoscaler scaled +2 nodes for rt-infer-us-east at 5187654338 • p99 decreased from 1.6s -> 1.05s (partial improvement)
Alexa Chen: Seeing improvement but still borderline for some flows. Jordan — go ahead with weighted routing to q4f16 for non-SLA customers now. Command: `routing set-weight text-gen-us-east --variant v1-q4f16 --weight 0.4`
Jordan Patel: Done. Weighted routing applied. Observing p99 -> 760ms overall, errors down to ~1.2%.
Alexa Chen: Great. Actions to document in the handoff: 
- Primary status: Alexa Chen (ACTIVE) — scaled pool and initiated routing fallback
- Secondary: Jordan Patel (MONITOR) — applied routing, watching metrics
- Coverage gaps: No one on-call in APAC for cross-region failover; gap-note added to rotation: https://redwood.internal/oncall/coverage-gaps
- Runbooks referenced: kvcache-warmup, pod-oom-restart, routing-weight-fallback (links above + https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-weight-fallback)
- Next steps for follow-up shift: check for root cause of OOM regressions (likely sidecar mem), correlate deploys 30m prior (deploy-rt-infer 5179991111)
Mia Torres: I’ll create a brief incident summary for the post-handoff: impact window, affected customers, mitigation steps, routing delta, and next RCA owner. Assigning RCA to Samir.
Samir Gupta: Acknowledged. I’ll start by rolling back the sidecar change in staging then prod canary. Rollback runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-rollback
Alexa Chen: ok wrapping up primary window — leaving primary to Jordan in 10m unless anything else pops. Final note: if p99 regresses >1s, escalate to eng-runtime and paging for urgent-hotfix. :thumbsup:
